newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais, AmEx no comment on card deal report.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais, AmEx no comment on card deal report.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais and American Express Co declined to comment on Friday on a newspaper report that they are negotiating a deal to allow Lyonnais to issue Amex cards to employees of its corporate clients.
The article published in The Wall Street Journal Europe on Friday, citing banking executives, said an agreement between the two groups was imminent.
A Credit Lyonnais spokesman told Reuters, "We have strictly no comment about American Express" while an American Express spokeswoman in Paris said "We don't comment on speculation or rumour".

The report said a Lyonnais deal with American Express would be likely to cause an outcry from other French banks as it would be the first time a bank had broken ranks with the existing national payment card association set up in the early 1980s.
It said the Groupement Carte Bleue industry association, which represents French banks using Visa cards, was trying to stop the deal by presenting an alternative product.

A Groupement Carte Bleue official told Reuters he had nothing to say about whether Lyonnais was having discussions with other parties, but said the association had been in talks with the French bank about its own version of a corporate card for several weeks.
He said five French banks, BNP, Banques populaires, Credit Commercial de France, Credit du Nord and BFCE, had adopted the Carte Bleue corporate card.
